query: AlCrFeNiSi belongs to a high-entropy-alloy family developed to combine properties that traditional single-principal-element alloys often cannot achieve simultaneously. Earlier research sought stable solid solutions and adjusted HEA compositions to target particular properties, but tradeoffs persisted: the CoCrFeMnNi system has limited wear and corrosion resistance, manganese can promote oxidation and oxide spallation, and cobalt-containing systems raise cost and processability concerns. Conventional bulk fabrication can cause compositional segregation during cooling, whereas mainstream metallic additive-manufacturing techniques can generate residual thermal stresses that impair mechanical performance and increase processing complexity. Given cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock, what single intervention could improve mechanical integrity while limiting segregation, residual stress, and defect formation? State one hypothesis containing the intervention, its causal mechanism, a quantitative or directional outcome relative to conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi, the processing and test boundaries of validity, the prior evidence supporting it, and a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The use of selective laser melting (SLM) additive manufacturing with optimized process parameters can improve the mechanical integrity of AlCrFeNiSi high-entropy alloy by reducing segregation, residual stress, and defect formation compared to conventional bulk fabrication methods.
generation.intervention: Selective laser melting (SLM) additive manufacturing with optimized process parameters
generation.conditions: Optimized process parameters, such as laser power, scanning speed, and powder layer thickness, to minimize residual stress and defect formation
generation.structural_mediator: Densification and microstructure refinement during SLM processing
generation.mechanism: Reduced segregation and residual stress due to the rapid solidification and controlled cooling rates inherent in SLM processing, leading to improved mechanical properties
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved mechanical integrity, including increased strength, ductility, and resistance to wear and corrosion, compared to conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi
generation.baseline: Conventional bulk fabrication methods, such as casting and machining
generation.boundary: Limited to the specific AlCrFeNiSi composition and SLM process parameters optimized for this alloy system
generation.uncertainty: The exact relationship between SLM process parameters and the resulting microstructure and mechanical properties of AlCrFeNiSi is not fully understood and requires further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Comparative study of the mechanical properties of AlCrFeNiSi fabricated using SLM additive manufacturing and conventional bulk fabrication methods
measurements: Microstructural analysis using SEM and EBSD
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the SLM-fabricated AlCrFeNiSi exhibits significantly lower mechanical properties or increased segregation and defect formation compared to the conventionally fabricated alloy, the hypothesis is falsified

High-entropy alloys (HEAs) present a new approach of alloying concepts. Whereas conventional alloys usually comprise one major alloying element and minor additions of other alloying elements to improve properties, HEAs consist of at least five elements with close to equimolar composition. For several compositions, the desired formation of solely solid solutions with a face-centred cubic (fcc) or a body-centred cubic (bcc) structure could be achieved [ [1] , [2] , [3] ].

Several groups of HEAs have been intensively investigated. The term compositionally complex alloys (CCAs) was introduced for HEAs with a multiphase microstructure [ [4] ]. Several investigations prove the formation of primarily cubic phases in the alloy AlCoCrCuFeNi and its derivatives [ [5] , [6] , [7] ]. Aluminium strongly influences the microstructure, phase formation and resulting properties. Furthermore, aluminium acts as a stabiliser of bcc solid solutions and can suppress the formation of complex phases [ [8] , [9] , [10] ]. One of the most promising and progressive fields in modern material science is high-entropy alloys (HEAs). The first to propose HEAs’ concept was J.W. Yeh [ [1] ], but since then, it has changed rather significantly, especially during the last few years [ [2] ]. Due to their extremely high mechanical and physical properties, refractory HEAs are classified as a separate group of materials. Such alloying compositions mainly include elements from the IV, V, and VI columns of the periodic table with some additions of Al, Si, Ni, or Co [ [3] ].

First high-entropy equiatomic compositions based on refractory elements, such as NbMoTaW and NbMoTaWV, were obtained in prior research [ [4] , [5] ]. It was found that the alloys possess higher mechanical properties at higher temperatures in comparison to conventional superalloys, such as Inconel 718 and Haynes 230 [ [6] ]. It was also determined that the addition of V increases the hardness significantly (up to 11.4 GPa at 1150 °C) [ [7] ] and yield strength σ 0.2 from 1058 MPa to 1246 MPa [ [5] ]. The attractiveness of refractory high-entropy alloys (HEAs) as structural materials stems from their outstanding mechanical properties, thermal stability, wear resistance and corrosion performance in hostile environments [ [1] , [2] , [3] , [4] , [5] ]. Recently, refractory high-entropy alloys have received significant attention in relation to high-temperature application in aerospace, defense, and nuclear power generation industries [ [6] ]. In fact, they were designated to replace traditional Ni-based super-alloys in applications such as gas turbines, heat exchangers, aerospace propulsion components, rocket engine nozzle [ [7] ]. HEAs are multicomponent systems that are composed from a small number of principal elements. They are usually composed from at least five elements with individual atomic concentrations that range between 5% and 35%. HEAs can produce solid phase solutions, mainly due to their configurational entropy and ability to be adequately synthesized [ [8] , [9] , [10] ].
